SRC-038:R003.text: CORE-003 P1: Freshness proves only source-time freshness, not archive-policy freshness. A change in excludes, fidelity profile, sampling, size budget or overrides can make the existing archive semantically stale while all source mtimes remain older than the ZIP. The service then positively reports the wrong artifact as current.

SRC-038:R004.text: CORE-004 P1: The manifest's numeric source accounting is not accounting for the whole source tree whenever directory pruning occurs. A repository can omit a massive dependency/generated subtree while reporting files_excluded=0 for that subtree and source_bytes that exclude its contents. The directory is named, but the global-looking counters remain materially misleading.

SRC-038:R005.text: CORE-005 P1: The new transaction lock prevents simultaneous writes but does not protect the read-modify-write transaction used by campaign auto-repair. A stale resolver can legally acquire the lock after a newer writer and erase the newer campaign index state. This is a classic lost update and can regress UI progress/next-action state after a successful wave commit.

A valid Windows reference whose text casing differs from the stored filename can resolve successfully but still be ranked as unreferenced. Under a tight sample cap, a runtime/build-referenced media asset can therefore be omitted while an arbitrary unreferenced asset is retained.

SRC-038:R008.text: W2-001 P1: The request is canonically resolved once, but downstream lifecycle operations revert to the untrusted/raw optional request identity. A legal v2 name-only completion can therefore close an unrelated live project when one project's display name equals another project's canonical ID. That can free the wrong worker/lane, suppress its legitimate audit, and permit duplicate dispatch. The same identity loss silently prevents canonical project mirroring for name-only submissions.

SRC-038:R009.text: W2-002 P1: Lifecycle recovery treats a coarse wall-clock display timestamp as transaction ordering authority. Equal timestamps are common, not pathological. A crash during archive or restore can consequently roll a completed transition backward and delete the intended destination copy, violating the documented destination-first recovery invariant.

SRC-038:R010.text: W2-003 P1: The recently hardened exclusive-copy fallback and the transaction recovery protocol disagree about what constitutes successful publication. Recovery understands only hard-link identity. A crash in the fallback's final window converts a valid durable canonical layer into an orphan and causes duplicate audit delivery on retry.

A deliberately throttled RETRYABLE job becomes ordinary immediately claimable QUEUED work, so restarting the bridge/service accelerates retries and defeats the anti-pinball policy precisely during repeated startup failures.

SRC-038:R012.text: W2-005 P2: The copy-then-remove rename is neither failure-atomic nor recoverable. A transient Windows sharing violation after destination publication converts one audit into two canonical layers, while the API reports failure and its normal retry path cannot finish the original operation. Both copies may then be independently dispatched or implemented.

SRC-038:R013.text: PERF-001 P1: Freshness checking still executes packing-grade source analysis. The common unchanged path walks the project twice and may parse megabytes of source text; the nested-change path can do that planning work and then repeat it for the actual pack. Cancellation cannot interrupt the preflight. Cost therefore scales directly with project size even when the only requested answer is "reuse this ZIP?", and a cancel can appear ignored while the planner finishes.

As STANDARD/DEEP/FULL now retain more images/audio/video/fonts, this can dominate packing latency and CPU load. The compressor can literally work harder to create a larger artifact, an impressive little triumph of machinery over common sense.

The top-10 omitted report additionally pays O(n log n) sorting for a fixed ten-element output.
